newsitem.title: USA: California insurer to pay $1 mln for claims violations.
newsitem.headline: California insurer to pay $1 mln for claims violations.

text.p: Insurer INSCO/DICO Group will pay a $1 million fine to settle charges that one of its units, Indemnity Company of California, routinely delayed and withheld claims payments, state officials said Tuesday.
California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said the fine was one of the three largest penalties ever assessed against an insurance company by the Department of Insurance.

Responding to an unusually high number of complaints, the Insurance Department began a market conduct investigation of INSCO/DICO Group, an Orange County, Calif.-based company that sells surety bonds, in June 1994, the department said.
Insurance investigators reviewed hundreds of claims files and discovered a pattern of delay in processing claims and unjustfied denial of payment, the Insurance Department said.

In addition to the fine, which will be paid into the state's general fund, the company has agreed to stop any illegal claims-handling practices and pay $30,000 to reimburse the Insurance Department its legal expenses.
INSCO/DICO did not contest the penalty, the Department of Insurance said.

"I am confident the company is taking the measures necessary to remedy the practices that led to this investigation," Quackenbush said. "But to make sure, we'll be conducting a follow-up examination in the coming months."
The companies that make up the INSCO/DICO Group are owned by Surety Holdings Ltd.
